To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we observe a strong wake field induced by channeled heavy projectiles in a crystal, with a shift of the energy level of the order of 100 eV and an increase of the radiative electron capture probability by 20-50% with respect to the non-perturbed case.

the electron gas polarization effect induced in silicon crystals by heavy H-like projectiles of moderate velocities chaneled along a <100> axis is characterized by: (i) A shift of the continuum level by about 100 eV and an increase of the electron density by 10–20% with respect to the unperturbed values, (ii) the energy shift is in good agreement with the predictions of the linear response theory whereas the density enhancement is much weaker than expected.
we have observed the electron gas polarization induced by heavy H- like ions of moderate velocities (20 MeV/u and 13 Me V/u) channeled in Si crystals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of electron gas polarization effects induced by heavy ions of moderate velocities.
the interaction of swift heavy ions with solid targets.
the study of electron gas polarization by fast heavy ions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron gas polarization induced by heavy ions channeled at moderate velocities is not a localized phenomenon.

our results show that the wake effect induced by the heavy ions channeled along a silicon channeling axis is a collective response of the electron gas, which is not fully described by the linear response theory.
our experimental data show that the electron gas polarization effect is not only present, but also that it can be very large for moderate values of the adibaticity parameter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we observe a strong perturbation in the electron density of the crystal, which induces a shift of more than 100 eV of the continuum level and an increase of the radiative electron capture probability.
the wake effect is a very efficient perturbation mechanism, but the density enhancement is smaller than predicted by linear response theory.

the electron gas polarization is strongly modified by a heavy ion moving in the crystal at moderate velocity, but that the electron density enhancement is not as important as predicted by the linear response theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron gas polarization effect can be used to probe the electron density in the vicinity of a moving ion, even in the non-adiabatic regime.
heavy ions channeled at moderate velocities can strongly perturb the electron density of a solid.
, in the case of heavy ions, the electron gas response to the passage of a charged particle can be very different from what was observed for protons or light ions.
